newsitem.title: ITALY: ALPINE SKIING-VON GRUENIGEN WINS GIANT SLALOM.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-VON GRUENIGEN WINS GIANT SLALOM.

text.p: Switzerland's Michael von Gruenigen clinched his first World Cup win of the season on Sunday with victory in a giant slalom on Sunday.
The World Cup giant slalom champion clocked an unofficial combined time of two minutes 32.66 seconds to lead home a Swiss one-two with compatriot Steve Locher in second place.
Locher, winner of the opening giant slalom of the season in Austria in October, clocked 2:33.43 ahead of Italian newcomer Matteo Nana who was third in 2:34.15.
Austria's Hans Knauss retains the overall World Cup lead through Christmas after his closest rival and compatriot Thomas Sykora skied out on the first leg.
Sunday's race was the last before the Christmas holiday break. The men's World Cup circuit reopens with a downhill at the Italian resort of Bormio on December 29.
